name: Compute summary statistics of diffusion measures mapped to visual regions binned by eccentricity - Benson14
summary: Computes mean diffusion measures and FreeSurfer anatomical measures (thickness, surface area, volume) within Benson14 visual areas binned by pRF eccentricity, and outputs parc-stats CSVs.
description: Takes the Benson14 retinotopy surfaces (visual area and eccentricity maps) from the prf input, binarises the eccentricity map into the requested bins, combines them with the visual-area labels to build eccentricity-binned annotations, and then runs FreeSurfer mri_segstats on each cortex-mapped measure and mris_anatomical_stats on each annotation. Use it to compare diffusion or anatomical measures across visual areas and eccentricity ranges. It needs a cortexmap, the FreeSurfer subject directory and the Benson14 prf output of the same subject. minDegree and maxDegree must list the same number of space-separated values.

inputs.description: Cortex-mapped measures for the subject (func/ directory of per-hemisphere .func.gii measure files).
FreeSurfer subject directory of the same subject; its white surfaces are used to convert maps and compute anatomical statistics.
Benson14 retinotopy output providing per-hemisphere varea (visual area) and eccentricity surface maps.

outputs.description: CSV files of diffusion and anatomical statistics for each eccentricity-binned visual-area parcellation.
Intermediate text, CSV, GIFTI and annotation files kept for debugging.

parameters.description: Space-separated lower bounds of the eccentricity bins (for example '0 7' for bins 0-5 and 7-90).
Space-separated upper bounds of the eccentricity bins, paired with minDegree (for example '5 90').

failure_modes.cause: No FreeSurfer license in the environment.
failure_modes.fix: Set the FREESURFER_LICENSE environment variable on the compute resource.

failure_modes.message: stats computations failed somewhere. please check logs and derivatives
failure_modes.fix: Check the log; make sure minDegree and maxDegree have the same number of values.
